clips.send: Atlanta. Railroad hub, “capital of the New South”. The 1867–68 convention met here and moved the capital from Milledgeville to Atlanta. Home of the International Cotton Exposition (1881) and the Cotton States Exposition (1895). Black colleges grew here: Atlanta University, Morehouse, Spelman, Clark. W. E. B. Du Bois taught at Atlanta University (1897–1910). Site of the 1906 race massacre and the 1913 Leo Frank trial.

clips.send: A sharecropper owned almost nothing: the landowner supplied land, mule, tools and seed and took about half the cotton. A tenant farmer owned a mule and tools and paid rent (cash or about a quarter of the crop), so kept more — but paid his own costs. Both usually bought on credit under a “crop lien”: the crop was promised to the merchant before it was even grown.

clips.send: 1913 年，亚特兰大一家铅笔厂的犹太裔经理利奥·弗兰克被控谋杀 13 岁的女工玛丽·费根。证据薄弱，报纸却充满反犹言论，他仍被判死刑。1915 年斯莱顿州长把死刑减为终身监禁，随后一群暴徒把弗兰克从米利奇维尔的监狱劫走并在玛丽埃塔将他私刑处死。
